title: CDW19S coordinates phasic end processing via distinct enzymatic activities.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: There are no data files to open. I read the open-access full text (119,336 characters) including its data availability statement and methods; searched the whole text for accessions (none found); queried NCBI's cross-link service for this PubMed ID 42406631 (only PMC full text, no GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample or dbGaP entries); searched PRIDE (the European proteomics repository) and Zenodo (a general data archive) and both returned zero records. The Europe PMC supplementary-file listing timed out on two attempts, so the supplement itself is not retrievable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: What the four supplementary tables contain comes from the methods text alone: Table S1 = plasmids, Table S2 = small interfering RNA (siRNA) sequences, Table S3 = antibodies, Table S4 = quantitative PCR (polymerase chain reaction) primers. These are reagent lists, not measurement tables. The paper's claim that 'source data are provided with the paper' is also unverified, since I could not list the supplement.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. The data availability statement reads verbatim: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request.' That is the explicit A1 fail condition. No accession numbers appear anywhere in the text, NCBI reports no linked GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample record, and PRIDE and Zenodo searches returned nothing.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. Nothing resembling a prediction target exists as a column. The paper's measurements are western blot bands, immunofluorescence focus counts, metaphase chromosome spreads and quantitative PCR repair-pathway fold changes, reported only inside figure panels. Any label would have to be constructed by reading numbers off images.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. No feature matrix of any kind. The only sequence-like content is short siRNA and PCR primer sequences in reagent tables, which describe experimental tools rather than items to be modelled.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable, therefore recorded as fail. With no data table there is no units column; the figure quantifications are relative fold changes and arbitrary intensity units defined per panel.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. This is a mechanistic cell-biology study on a handful of human cell lines (HEK293T, a WDR70 knockout line, L02, T43), with experiments at the scale of tens of conditions and three or so biological replicates each. Nowhere near the ~1,500 labelled rows the checklist requires, and I verified no row count because no table exists.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially passes, but only because there is essentially no data. The whole supplement is reagent lists and figure images.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable, therefore recorded as fail. There is no download whose counts could be compared against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable, therefore recorded as fail. No label exists to trace. For completeness: the paper's underlying measurements are genuine physical assays (blots, microscopy, PCR), not another model's output, so circularity is not the problem here — absence of any released measurement table is.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no dataset, so no model can be trained or evaluated on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: No viable project; the paper describes a repair-protein mechanism but releases no measurement table to learn from.
plain_idea.train_on: Nothing usable. The project I considered was predicting how far a cell chews back a broken DNA end (DNA end resection) from which repair proteins are present, but the paper provides zero rows of such data; number of examples available is zero.
plain_idea.predict: Would have been the extent of single-stranded DNA produced at a double-strand break, measured by microscopy of a single-stranded-DNA-binding protein's foci. Those measurements exist only inside the paper's figure panels, not as released numbers.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: The biology matters — resection length decides whether a cell repairs a break accurately by homologous recombination or uses an error-prone route, which is central to how BRCA1-mutant tumours respond to therapy — but this paper contributes no data that would let anyone model it.

ml_idea: None viable. A machine-learning project would need a table of DNA-break repair outcomes across many genetic conditions, for example a pooled CRISPR screen scoring resection or repair-pathway choice for thousands of gene knockouts. This paper is a low-throughput mechanistic study of one protein complex and supplies no such table.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no dataset. The 0.05 GB figure is my estimate of the supplement's total size (reagent tables plus figure images), not a measured value.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement. It says data are available 'from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request', which kills A1 in one sentence. Total cost: one minute.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright: the data availability statement is 'available from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request', and I confirmed there is no deposit in GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, PRIDE or Zenodo, and no accession number anywhere in the text. A2, A3 and A5 fail too. This is a low-throughput mechanistic cell-biology paper — western blots, immunofluorescence focus counts, chromosome spreads and quantitative PCR repair assays on four human cell lines — whose only supplementary tables are lists of plasmids, small interfering RNAs, antibodies and PCR primers. There is no feature/label table, no prediction target as a column, and nothing close to the ~1,500 labelled rows required. Excellent mechanistic biology, no machine-learning substrate.
